reason_for_addition: The frozen exchangeability test showed strong size-selective durable extinction. Because small groups can hit zero under individual-independent stochastic thinning even without social facilitation, an explicit size-dependent mechanistic null is required before interpreting that result biologically.
question: Is the observed size selectivity of durable colony-code disappearance stronger than expected from proportional individual-independent thinning alone?

null_model.scope: Each event-bearing island-year risk set is treated separately.
null_model.rate: lambda = total next-year count among labeled at-risk colony codes / total prior-year count among those colony codes.
null_model.count_model: For colony i, next-year count is Poisson(lambda * prior_count_i).
null_model.conditioning: Condition on the observed number k of durable-extinction events in each risk set. Under independent Poisson counts, event identities are sampled with conditional subset weight proportional to product_i[q_i/(1-q_i)] over the k selected colonies.
null_model.statistic: The same equal-risk-set standardized prior-size contrast used by the frozen hazard contract.

directional_test.excess_small_group_vulnerability: Observed contrast more negative than the proportional-thinning null.
directional_test.lower_tail_p: Monte Carlo lower-tail p with +1 correction.
directional_test.interpretation: Only a lower-tail deviation would support size selectivity beyond proportional demographic stochasticity.

interpretation_boundaries: This analysis was designed after the exchangeability result was known and is exploratory falsification, not preregistered confirmation.
Failure to exceed the thinning null argues against using size-selective disappearance itself as evidence for social facilitation, predation or an Allee effect.
The Poisson model is a deliberately simple individual-independent benchmark, not a complete demographic process model.
A separate reproductive-success analysis is required to test whether small groups have lower chicks per breeding pair.
